page_title: GitHub issue olake#1317: CI: commit go.sum and go.work.sum, and fail lint when go.mod is not tidy
text:
Issue (completed): About 1 in 14 CI run attempts since August had a driver image build fail with `reading https://sum.golang.org/tile/...: stream error: ... INTERNAL_ERROR; received from peer` ([example](https://github.com/datazip-inc/olake/actions/runs/38752537764/job/116508541502?pr=1137)).
`go.sum` and `go.work.sum` are gitignored, so every cold-cache build sends about 3,400 requests to sum.golang.org and fails if any one of them errors. With the sums committed, the same build sends none.

### Targets

- [ ] Commit `go.sum` for every module (`make gomod`) and both `go.work.sum` files (root and `tests/`), and remove them from `.gitignore`. `go mod tidy` does not write `go.work.sum`. A workspace build or `go list` fills it, and at HEAD that is 2 lines once the modules are tidy.
- [ ] Make `make olake.lint` and `make test.lint` first run `go mod tidy -diff` in every module they lint, and fail with `go.mod/go.sum not tidy in <dir>: run make gomod and commit the result` when it prints a diff. CI already runs both targets. The pre-commit hook skips `olake.lint` unless a `.go` file changed, so it should also trigger on `go.mod` and `go.sum` changes.

### How other repos do it

- `go mod tidy -diff` (Go 1.23+) prints the needed changes and exits non-zero without touching any file ([Go 1.23 release notes](https://go.dev/doc/go1.23)).
- golangci-lint runs `go mod tidy --diff` as a PR check ([pr-checks.yml](https://github.com/golangci/golangci-lint/blob/HEAD/.github/workflows/pr-checks.yml)).
- OpenTel…

Discussion:

- contributor: My plan for fixing this issue is to:

- Remove `go.sum` and `go.work.sum` from `.gitignore` and commit the required checksum files for all Go modules and workspaces.
- Update `make olake.lint` and `make test.lint` to run `go mod tidy -diff` for each relevant module, with a clear error message if dependencies are not tidy.
- Update `.githooks/pre-commit` to trigger the appropriate lint checks when `go.mod` or `go.sum` files change.

I’ll verify the changes by running `make gomod`, generating the workspace checksum files, and testing both lint targets.

This should help reduce unnecessary checksum database requests in CI and keep dependency files consistent.

page_title: GitHub issue olake#1306: Postgres ctid chunk splitter ignores TOAST, producing enormous chunks (~11 h each) so an interrupted sync commits nothing
text:
Issue (completed): ## Summary

For a Postgres table whose size is dominated by TOASTed `jsonb`, the ctid splitter sizes chunks from
`relpages` (main heap only). TOAST is a separate relation and is invisible to that calculation, so a
4.5 TB table was split into **9 chunks** that OLake believed were 2 GB each but which actually carried
**~1.2 TB / ~9.8M rows** each — a ~640x underestimate.

Because the Iceberg commit happens once per chunk at writer close, the first possible commit was ~11
hours in. Two runs were interrupted before any chunk completed, so **12.5 hours of reading produced 0
committed rows** (0 snapshots on the destination table) and no resumable state.

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| OLake | v0.12.0 (`olakego/source-postgres:v0.12.0`) |
| Source | PostgreSQL 18.4, `update_method: Standalone`, `max_threads: 2`, `retry_count: 5` |
| Destination | Iceberg, REST catalog (Lakekeeper 0.10.4), S3-compatible (Wasabi), legacy writer (`arrow_writes` unset) |
| Deployment | OLake UI + workers on GKE (olake-helm) |
| Stream | Full Refresh + Incremental, cursor `id`, no `chunk_column` |

## Source table profile

```
rows          : 78,523,153
main heap     :    16 GB      <- what relpages measures
TOAST         : 4,488 GB      <- two jsonb columns
indexes       :    23 GB
total         : 4,527 GB
avg payload   : ~131 KB of JSON per row
rows per page : ~37  (78.5M rows / 2,097,152 heap pages)
```

## What happens

`drivers/postgres/internal/backfill.go` (`generateCTIDRanges`, non-partitioned…

Discussion:

- collaborator: @AvinashKumar0923 please try out the olake version `0.12.1` and verify if the fix is working for you

- none: > 2\. [@AvinashKumar0923](https://github.com/AvinashKumar0923) please try out the olake version `0.12.1` and verify if the fix is working for you

Thanks @mihir-datazip for the quick fix in #1309.

I haven’t re-run this table on 0.12.1 yet. My backfill already finished using the chunk_column: id workaround, and I didn’t want to re-read 4.5 TB just to verify. I went through the PR against this table’s profile, and the numbers match: PG 18 takes the TID-range path, and table-size-based page sizing gives about 931 pages per chunk, about 2,251 chunks of about 35K rows each. At our measured throughput that means a commit roughly every 1.5–3 min instead of every ~11 h. A preemption like run 2’s would then lose at most the in-flight chunks rather than the whole 12.5 h. Using live pg_relation_size instead of relpages also removes the stale-ANALYZE concern I raised.

One note for anyone upgrading mid-backfill: existing state.json chunks are reused, so the state needs clearing for the new sizing to apply.

Closing this one; I’ll reopen if the next full refresh on 0.12.1 shows anything off.

page_title: GitHub issue olake#1242: kafka discover: ProduceSchema discards fetch and schema-resolution errors, silently producing an empty or partial schema
text:
Issue (completed): ## Summary

`ProduceSchema` drops errors at two levels, so a topic whose messages could not be fetched or resolved is reported as a successfully-discovered stream with a missing or incomplete schema.

## The path

In `drivers/kafka/internal/kafka.go:249-265`:

```go
_ = k.processKafkaMessages(ctx, reader, func(record types.KafkaRecord) (bool, error) {
    messageCount++
    if record.Data != nil {
        mu.Lock()
        err := typeutils.Resolve(stream, record.Data)
        mu.Unlock()
        if err != nil {
            return true, err   // (a) propagated to processKafkaMessages...
        }
    }
    shouldExit := messageCount >= 10000 || record.Message.Offset >= endOffset.Offset-1
    return shouldExit, nil
})
return nil                      // (b) ...and then thrown away here
```

- **(a) → (b)**: `typeutils.Resolve` failures are returned from the callback, `processKafkaMessages` propagates them, and the `_ =` assignment discards the result.
- The per-partition closure then unconditionally `return nil`, so `utils.Concurrent` sees every partition as successful and the `if err != nil` check at line 267 can never fire for these causes.
- The same discard hides fetch-side failures: `processKafkaMessages` wraps genuine fetch errors as `constants.ErrNonRetryable` (`drivers/kafka/internal/cdc.go:271-273`), and those are discarded too.

## Impact

Discover reports success for a topic it could not actually read. The resulting stream has no resolved columns beyond the `_kafka_*`…

Discussion:

- collaborator: @maltzsama thanks for flagging this. We are looking into it and will get back shortly.

- collaborator: @maltzsama Discover samples the first 10,000 messages to infer the stream schema. Columns that appear later are handled by schema evolution during sync, so a partial sample does not block the pipeline. Non-JSON messages are skipped during sampling. Could you let us know if this has caused any problems on your side?

page_title: GitHub issue olake#1241: kafka: ReaderManager.exitMode is never reset and is shared by all readers, so one rebalance halts every reader for the rest of the sync
text:
Issue (completed): ## Summary

`ReaderManager.exitMode` (`pkg/kafka/types.go:41`) is a single `atomic.Int32` on the manager, shared by every reader in the group. Two problems follow from that.

### 1. It is never reset

`exitMode` is only ever written to a *terminal* value — `gracefulExit` or `nonRetryableExit` (`pkg/kafka/reader.go:316`, `pkg/kafka/reader.go:323`). Nothing ever stores `normalProcessing` back. `RestartReader` recreates the franz-go client but leaves `exitMode` untouched (`pkg/kafka/reader.go:273-292`).

So once any rebalance fires, every subsequent retry attempt short-circuits immediately: `processKafkaMessages` checks `FetchExitState()` before its first poll (`drivers/kafka/internal/cdc.go:250-252`) and returns straight away. The retry driven by `RetryOnBackoff` (`utils/utils.go:482`) burns its attempts without ever reading a record.

### 2. It is global, not per-reader

The driver runs readers in parallel — `ChangeStreamConfig` returns `parallel=true` (`drivers/kafka/internal/cdc.go:24-26`), and `drivers/abstract/cdc.go:82` fans out one goroutine per reader index. All of them share one `ReaderManager` and therefore one `exitMode`.

A rebalance callback on **one** reader sets the flag for **all** of them. Readers that still hold valid, unaffected partition assignments stop mid-partition too. Combined with issue #1240 (graceful exit reported as success → offsets committed), a single rebalance on one reader can cause short reads to be committed across every partition in the sync…

Discussion:

- collaborator: @maltzsama thanks for flagging this. We are looking into it and will get back shortly.

- collaborator: @maltzsama Sharing exitMode across readers, and not resetting it after a rebalance, is by design.

When a rebalance is detected, we gracefully stop the sync. At that point, all readers need to stop consuming further records; otherwise, there is a risk of duplicate processing because their partition assignments may no longer be valid.

During the retry, static membership prevents another rebalance from being triggered. As a result, the exit mode is not changed back at that point, and the readers continue with the existing exit state.

- collaborator: Closing this issue due to inactivity. Please feel free to reopen it if it's still relevant or if further work is needed.

page_title: GitHub issue olake#1240: kafka: graceful rebalance exit is reported as success, committing offsets for partitions that were never fully read
text:
Issue (completed): ## Summary

When a consumer group rebalance is detected mid-sync, the Kafka driver stops processing and reports **success**, which causes `PostCDC` to commit offsets. Because the partitions were only partially consumed, the unread remainder is skipped permanently on the next run.

## The path

1. `kgo.OnPartitionsAssigned` / `OnPartitionsRevoked` fire → `r.exitMode.Store(gracefulExit)` (`pkg/kafka/reader.go:312-318`).
2. `FetchExitState()` returns `(stop=true, err=nil)` for `gracefulExit` (`pkg/kafka/reader.go:359-361`).
3. `processKafkaMessages` sees `stopProcessing==true, err==nil` and returns `nil` (`drivers/kafka/internal/cdc.go:250-252`).
4. `StreamChanges` gets `err == nil`, so it skips the error return and proceeds to build `metadataByStream` from whatever landed in `lastMessages` (`drivers/kafka/internal/cdc.go:146-171`).
5. `streamChanges` in `drivers/abstract/cdc.go:107-111` runs the deferred `PostCDC` — which calls `reader.CommitRecords(ctx, messages...)` (`drivers/kafka/internal/cdc.go:218`).

The committed offset is the last record processed *before the rebalance interrupted us*, not the partition end offset. On the next sync `PartitionsForStream` skips everything at or below that committed offset (`pkg/kafka/reader.go:139-142`), so the records between the interrupt point and `EndOffset` are never read.

A rebalance is a normal, expected event (a member joining/leaving, a session timeout, a coordinator move). Treating it as a clean completion turns a routine even…

Discussion:

- collaborator: @maltzsama thanks for flagging this. We are looking into it and will get back shortly.

- collaborator: @maltzsama The statement that the records between the interruption point and `EndOffset` are never read is not correct. The committed offset is intentionally the last successfully processed record before the rebalance, rather than the partition's `EndOffset`.

On the next sync, `PartitionsForStream` resumes from the committed offset, so records after the interruption point are still consumed. We also emit a `Warnf` log when the sync is stopped gracefully.

This behavior is intentional and ensures that rebalances are handled safely without data loss.

- collaborator: Closing this issue due to inactivity. Please feel free to reopen it if it's still relevant or if further work is needed.

page_title: GitHub issue olake#1239: kafka source: Avro/Protobuf wire-format messages silently mis-decoded as JSON when schema_registry is not configured
text:
Issue (completed): ## Summary

`drivers/kafka/internal/cdc.go` `parseKafkaData`/`parseData` detects Confluent wire-format messages (`isConfluentWireFormat`, magic byte `0x00` + 4-byte schema ID) but when `schema_registry` is not configured, it unconditionally treats the payload as JSON:

```go
if isConfluentWireFormat(data) {
    if k.schemaRegistryClient == nil {
        return decodeJSONMessage(data[5:])
    }
    ...
```

If the topic actually contains Avro- or Protobuf-encoded data (which is the common case when wire-format framing is present at all — plain JSON producers rarely emit the magic byte), this attempts to JSON-decode raw binary Avro/Protobuf bytes. Best case this fails with a confusing `invalid character ...` JSON parse error that gives no hint that a schema registry is required; worst case (rare, if the binary happens to start with valid JSON-parseable bytes) it could produce garbage decoded data silently, which is worse than a clean failure.

Yes, a Kafka source can be configured today without `schema_registry` (`Config.SchemaRegistry *kafka.SchemaRegistryClient` is optional and `Validate()` only checks it when non-nil, see `drivers/kafka/internal/config.go:62-66`). That's a legitimate mode for JSON topics without wire-format framing — this issue is only about the case where wire-format framing IS detected but no registry is present to resolve it.

## Suggested fix

When `isConfluentWireFormat(data)` is true and `k.schemaRegistryClient == nil`, return a clear, actionable error…

Discussion:

- collaborator: @maltzsama thanks for flagging this. We are looking into it and will get back shortly.

- collaborator: @maltzsama  treating Confluent-framed messages as JSON when schema_registry is not configured is by design. We cannot reliably determine whether a message is JSON or Avro just by looking at the message, since JSON does not have a fixed schema. We use sampling to infer the JSON schema, and this behavior was implemented accordingly. Could you let us know if this has caused any problems on your side?

page_title: GitHub issue olake#1189: arrow_writes: true breaks CDC deduplication on Iceberg/Glue destination — no equality-delete written, rows physically duplicate on every UPDATE
text:
Issue (completed): **Title:** `arrow_writes: true` breaks CDC deduplication on Iceberg/Glue destination — no equality-delete written, rows physically duplicate on every UPDATE

## Environment
- OLake UI: v0.5.0 (`olakego/ui`)
- OLake worker: v0.3.10 (`olakego/ui-worker`)
- Source connector: `olakego/source-mysql:v0.9.5`
- Source: MySQL 8.0 (Aurora MySQL 3.10), CDC via binlog (`ROW`, `FULL` row image, GTID on)
- Destination: Iceberg via Glue catalog, S3 storage
- Deployment: official `docker-compose.yaml` from the OLake repo, minimal profile (no Fusion/Amoro optimizer running)

## Summary
With the destination config `writer.arrow_writes: true`, any row that receives more than one CDC event in short succession (e.g. an application `INSERT` immediately followed by an `UPDATE`, a very common pattern — create a record, then fill in a few more fields moments later) gets written as **two separate physical rows** in the Iceberg table, with **no equality-delete file ever produced** to mark the older version as superseded. A plain `SELECT * FROM table` returns both versions forever. Setting `writer.arrow_writes: false` (Legacy writer) on an otherwise identical destination fixes this completely.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Configure a MySQL source with `sync_mode: strict_cdc` (or `cdc`) on a table with `source_defined_primary_key: ["id"]`, `default_stream_properties.append_mode: false`.
2. Configure an Iceberg/Glue destination with `arrow_writes: true`.

Source drivers and `ReformatDate` keep full microseconds. The digits are lost only on the Go → Java gRPC hop of the legacy writer, and both sides assume milliseconds:

page_title: GitHub issue olake#1177: Iceberg destination: selected_columns excludes OLake metadata columns from CREATE-time schema, breaking _olake_id identifier field
text:
Issue (completed): ## Environment

- Olake version: v0.9.5 (also present on current `master` as of this report)
- Destination: Iceberg, REST catalog (AWS S3 Tables)
- Source: Postgres, CDC (pgoutput)

## Description

When a stream's `selected_columns.columns` is a non-empty allowlist, the Iceberg destination excludes OLake's own metadata columns (`_olake_id`, `_olake_timestamp`, `_op_type`, `_cdc_timestamp`) from the schema sent to the writer at `GET_OR_CREATE_TABLE` time, because they are never listed in the user's column allowlist. The table therefore gets created (or evolved) without `_olake_id`, with no identifier field at all.

Once real records are written, `_olake_id` (and the other three metadata columns) get merged into the row data regardless of `selected_columns` (`destination/iceberg/iceberg.go`, `FlattenAndCleanData`: `maps.Copy(records[idx].Data, record.OlakeColumns)`), so `_olake_id` shows up as a "new column" against the table's actual schema. Schema evolution then adds it as a new field on an existing table, and Iceberg requires new fields on an existing table to be optional. Right after that, OLake calls `UpdateSchema.setIdentifierFields(["_olake_id"])`, which throws:

```

	at org.apache.iceberg.Schema.validateIdentifierField(Schema.java:168)
```

This repeats on every retry (with backoff) because `GET_OR_CREATE_TABLE` loads the already-created, already-broken table rath…

page_title: GitHub issue olake#1175: Postgres CDC: unchanged TOAST values are lost should we read them back from the source?
text:
Issue (completed): ## TL;DR

When an `UPDATE` doesn't touch a large out-of-line (TOASTed) column, Postgres leaves that column out
of the WAL. OLake currently writes a placeholder string for such columns into the destination. One fix is to read the value back from the source through a held `REPEATABLE READ` transaction. **It works and it is provably correct, but we have measured what it costs and would like input before committing to it.** A second approach reconstructing the value from the destination is tracked in the companion issue and puts zero load on the source (here postgres database).

---

## 1. The problem

A tuple must fit in an 8 KB page. Postgres moves large variable-length values (`text`, `jsonb`,
`bytea`, …) into a companion TOAST table, leaving an 18-byte pointer behind. When you update a row
**without changing that column**, Postgres does not rewrite it, so there is nothing to put in the
WAL. Logical replication sends a marker instead:

> `Byte1('u')` "Identifies unchanged TOASTed value (the actual value is not sent)."
> [PostgreSQL protocol docs](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/16/protocol-logicalrep-message-formats.html)

This is exact, not a heuristic. The protocol tells us precisely which columns are affected.

### What OLake does today

`pkg/waljs/pgoutput.go` writes the literal string `__olake_unavailable_value__` into the column.

Before Postgres moves a value out of the row, **it tries to compress it first**. Only if the value is
*still* too large after compression does…

Discussion:

- collaborator: Closing in favor of #1176.
- Re-reading from the source needs a transaction held open for the whole CDC run, which stops vacuum from cleaning up.
- Measured on a busy source: 10× database growth, ~14× CPU per unit of work.
- OLake should not put extra load on the user's database.
- Unchanged TOAST values will be read back from the destination instead.

page_title: GitHub issue olake#1069: Postgres CDC cannot run against a read-replica: `pg_current_wal_lsn()` errors during recovery
text:
Issue (completed): ### What happens

Point the Postgres driver at a physical standby and every CDC run dies before any data moves:

```
failed to get slot position: ERROR: recovery is in progress (SQLSTATE 25006)
```

### Why

`pkg/waljs/replicator.go` builds the slot lookup with `pg_current_wal_lsn()`:

```go
ReplicationSlotTempl = "SELECT plugin, slot_type, confirmed_flush_lsn, pg_current_wal_lsn() as current_lsn FROM pg_replication_slots WHERE slot_name = '%s'"
```

That is a WAL control function, and it raises `recovery is in progress` on a standby. The standby equivalent is `pg_last_wal_replay_lsn()`. Nothing branches on `pg_is_in_recovery()`, so there is no path through this that works on a replica.

`GetSlotPosition` runs from `Postgres.PreCDC` (`drivers/postgres/internal/cdc.go`) on every CDC run, and again in the LSN wait loop in `replicator.go`, so it fires immediately rather than partway through a sync.

### Why it matters

Postgres 16 added logical decoding on standbys, so the slot can live on a replica and keep decode load off a busy primary. The rest of the driver already looks compatible: `pg_replication_slot_advance()` is allowed on a standby for slots local to it, and `IdentifySystem` returns the replay position there. This one expression is the whole blocker.

The MSSQL driver picked up read-replica support in #949 and #991. This is the Postgres counterpart.

### Reproduction

PostgreSQL 18, a streaming replica built with `pg_basebackup -R`, `wal_level=logical` and `hot_standb…

page_title: GitHub issue olake#1014: Bug: Concurrent record filtering causes out-of-order data corruption
text:
Issue (completed): ## Description
Concurrent filtering in `utils/typeutils/filter.go` scrambles record order. 
**Impact:** Processing CDC events out-of-order leads to data corruption (e.g., applying an older `UPDATE` after a newer one, or `DELETE` before `INSERT`).
## Steps to reproduce
1. Configure a pipeline with a filter.
2. Ingest a batch of ordered records.
3. Observe the output from `FilterRecords`—the records are shuffled due to non-deterministic goroutine execution and mutex locking.
## Expected behavior
Filtered records must strictly retain their original sequence.
## Actual behavior
Records are appended to the `filtered` slice randomly as goroutines complete.
## Proposed Solution
Instead of appending directly via a mutex, either:
1. Process records sequentially (safest/simplest).
2. Concurrently evaluate conditions into an index-mapped boolean array, then sequentially build the final filtered slice.

Discussion:

- none: Evaluating predicates concurrently into an index-addressed result array and compacting in a second ordered pass preserves sequence without giving up parallel predicate work. The implementation should also define how a predicate error or panic affects the batch: cancel remaining workers and return no partial reordered output, rather than silently dropping an index. A deterministic test can insert per-record delays in reverse order and verify that surviving CDC records retain their original sequence across many runs.

page_title: GitHub issue olake#984: Postgres CDC to S3 Parquet sets large jsonb / LOB column to null
text: Issue (completed): ## Summary When using Olake with PostgreSQL as the source and S3 Parquet as the destination, some `jsonb` columns are being written as `null` during CDC sync. This looks similar to the LOB/null column issue seen with AWS DMS. ## Environment - Source: PostgreSQL - Destination: S3 Parquet - Sync mode: CDC - Affected column type: `jsonb` - Example affected column: `invoice_details` ## Issue During CDC, the `jsonb` column becomes `null` in the destination Parquet files, even though the source PostgreSQL table contains non-null values. The affected `jsonb` values are relatively large. Most values in this column are around 3 KB to 15 KB. ## Expected behavior The `jsonb` column should be replicated correctly to S3 Parquet during CDC, preserving the original value from PostgreSQL. ## Actual behavior The `jsonb` column is written as `null` in the destination during CDC for affected rows. ## Impact This causes data loss in the destination because important JSON payloads are missing after CDC replication. Using append-only mode with query-side deduplication may work as a temporary workaround, but CDC mode should ideally preserve the full `jsonb` value. ## Questions 1. … Discussion: - collaborator: @Rtunc ,Thanks for reporting this issue and for the detailed investigation. Regarding your questions: 1. **Is there currently a size limit for jsonb / LOB columns in PostgreSQL CDC?** Large `jsonb` values can be affected during CDC because PostgreSQL WAL records may not contain the full value for TOASTed columns. In such cases, the column value may appear as `null` in the destination. https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/storage-toast.html 2. **Could this be related to PostgreSQL TOASTed values?** Yes, this is related to PostgreSQL TOAST handling for large column values. 3. **Is there any configuration to force Olake to fetch full values for large jsonb columns during CDC?** At the moment, Olake does not support fetching full TOASTed jsonb values during CDC. As a workaround, you can use append-only mode with query-side deduplication. Alternatively, if you're okay with enabling REPLICA IDENTITY FULL on the affected table, we can help you with a quick fix. 4. **Is support for large jsonb / LOB columns in CDC planned?** Yes, support for large TOASTed `jsonb` / LOB columns in CDC is planned and is something we intend to address in a future release. - collaborator: We have resolved this issue and merged the fix, so closing this issue if you have any query left then feel free to reopen.

> What exactly UI does to stop job that is running?

In OLake, A Job is a Temporal workflow (a process). When you click **Cancel Run**, the UI sends a cancellation request to the workflow. Once the workflow context is cancelled, the workflow begins shutting down gracefully and the job is cancelled.

Since all the threads belong to the same workflow, when the workflow context is cancelled all the connections to the database instance from that workflow are closed.

page_title: GitHub issue olake#926: improvement: wire SIGINT/SIGTERM into root context for graceful shutdown
text:
Issue (completed): ## Problem

OLake does not wire OS signals (`SIGINT` / `SIGTERM`) into its root `context.Context`. When the operating system delivers a clean-shutdown signal — Kubernetes pod eviction, Karpenter node consolidation, `docker stop`, or Ctrl-C in a dev shell — the process exits immediately, without giving the CDC / backfill / destination-writer paths any chance to reach their existing `ctx.Done()` branches.

### Evidence

Searching the tree for any signal handling:

```
$ git grep -nE 'signal\.Notify|os\.Interrupt|syscall\.SIG(INT|TERM|HUP)' -- ':!LICENCE'
(no matches)
```

Confirmed on current `master` (`v0.6.5`).

The root command is built from cobra's default background context:

- `protocol/root.go` declares `RootCmd = &cobra.Command{...}` with no `SetContext` / `ExecuteContext` anywhere, so `cmd.Context()` inside every subcommand is `context.Background()` that never cancels on signals.
- `connector.go:18` — `protocol.CreateRootCommand(true, driver).Execute()` — uses plain `Execute()` (not `ExecuteContext`).
- `protocol/root.go:85` — `connector = abstract.NewAbstractDriver(RootCmd.Context(), ...)` — so `AbstractDriver.GlobalCtxGroup` / `GlobalConnGroup` are also rooted on a background context.

Meanwhile, the CDC / read paths already branch on `ctx.Done()` and would unwind cleanly if the context were cancellable:

2. Create job that will use this destination
3. Add  any table to the list of streams
4. Run sync, it should finish correctly

- collaborator: @lkzcgfvf Since **clear-destination** is a destructive operation, we cannot allow it to fail in a partially completed state. In the event of an error, it should continue retrying indefinitely until the issue is resolved, ensuring consistency and preventing any half-applied changes. (This is an intended design decision)

In your case, as the clear-destination error is expected, we have an `api` to recover in-progress (failing) clear-destination operation. It cancels the `clear` operation and resumes the `sync` operation.

```bash
COOKIE_JAR="/tmp/olake.cookies"; trap 'rm -f "$COOKIE_JAR"' EXIT
curl --location --request POST 'http://localhost:8000/login' \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data-raw '{"username":"admin","password":"password"}' \
  --cookie-jar "$COOKIE_JAR"

curl -i --location --request POST 'http://localhost:8000/internal/project/123/jobs/<JOB_ID>/clear-destination/recover' \
  --cookie "$COOKIE_JAR"
```

> Note: Please update the hostname, port and the job_id as per your configuration.

page_title: GitHub issue olake#862: AcknowledgeLSN times out when ClientXLogPos regresses behind confirmed_flush_lsn
text:
Issue (completed): ## Description

`AcknowledgeLSN` in `pkg/waljs/replicator.go` times out with a fatal `"LSN not updated after 5 minutes"` error when `ClientXLogPos` is behind the replication slot's `confirmed_flush_lsn`.

This happens in production when replicating databases with uneven WAL write/flush rates. We observed this on our OLake v0.5.0 deployment.

## Root Cause

There are two interacting issues:

**1. `ClientXLogPos` can regress behind `confirmed_flush_lsn`**

In `pgoutput.go:97` and `waljs.go:89`, the PrimaryKeepaliveMessage handler blindly assigns:

```go
p.socket.ClientXLogPos = pkm.ServerWALEnd
```

`ServerWALEnd` carries the WAL *flush* position, which can lag behind the WAL *write* position. Meanwhile, `PreCDC` advances the slot to `pg_current_wal_lsn()` (the write position). This creates a window where `ClientXLogPos` (flush) < `confirmed_flush_lsn` (advanced to write position).

**2. `AcknowledgeLSN` uses strict equality polling**

```go
if slot.LSN == walPosition {
    return nil
}
```

When `walPosition` (ClientXLogPos) is behind `confirmed_flush_lsn`, PostgreSQL silently ignores the StandbyStatusUpdate because `confirmed_flush_lsn` cannot move backwards. The equality check never matches, and the function times out after 5 minutes.

## Production Evidence

From our deployment logs:

```

confirmed_flush_lsn:    E/D8EA31B8
IdentifySystem XLogPos: E/D8E19108  (flush position, 9MB behind)

Issue (completed): ## Bug Description

There is a write-ordering issue in `PostCDC` and `PreCDC` that causes OLake's persisted cursor (LSN) to advance **ahead** of the PostgreSQL replication slot's `confirmed_flush_lsn`. Once this happens, the `validateGlobalState` check triggers a non-retryable error requiring a full "clear destination" — which is destructive and operationally painful for large datasets.

## Root Cause

In [`drivers/postgres/internal/cdc.go:81-91`](https://github.com/datazip-inc/olake/blob/main/drivers/postgres/internal/cdc.go#L81-L91):

```go
func (p *Postgres) PostCDC(ctx context.Context, _ int) error {
    defer waljs.Cleanup(ctx, p.replicator.Socket())
    select {
    case <-ctx.Done():
        return ctx.Err()
    default:
        socket := p.replicator.Socket()
        p.state.SetGlobal(waljs.WALState{LSN: socket.ClientXLogPos.String()})  // ① writes to disk
        return waljs.AcknowledgeLSN(ctx, p.client, socket, false)              // ② tells PostgreSQL
    }
}
```

`SetGlobal()` calls `LogState()` which **synchronously writes the state file to disk** before `AcknowledgeLSN()` sends the `StandbyStatusUpdate` to PostgreSQL. If the process crashes, gets OOM-killed, or AcknowledgeLSN fails/times out between steps ① and ②:

- OLake's state file has LSN X (already flushed to disk)
- PostgreSQL's replication slot still has the old LSN Y (where Y < X)
- On restart, `validateGlobalState` detects the mismatch and returns a **non-retryable error**

text:
Issue (completed): ## Description

In MySQL, there can be a difference between the actual value stored in a column and the value displayed when running a `SELECT * FROM table` query.

For example, consider a `FLOAT` (float32) column in MySQL. A value inserted as `12345.678912345678` may be displayed as `12345.679` when queried using the MySQL CLI. This is due to MySQL’s default display formatting and rounding behavior for floating-point types.

However, when syncing this data using OLake’s Iceberg Writer or Parquet Writer, the value is captured as the actual stored value (`12345.678912345678`) rather than the rounded value shown in the MySQL CLI (`12345.679`).

This behavior should be corrected so that the synced data matches the value displayed by MySQL during a `SELECT` query, ensuring consistency between source reads and downstream data consumers.

Issue (completed): ### Problem

When trying to create a CDC task with a MariaDB RDS instance the version returned from Maria does not correlate to the appropriate MySQL version and the check within pkg/jdbc/jdbc.go returns the wrong command to determine whether CDC can be enabled on the task.

`query := utils.Ternary(majorVersion > 8 || (majorVersion == 8 && minorVersion >= 4), jdbc.MySQLMasterStatusQueryNew(), jdbc.MySQLMasterStatusQuery()).(string)`

In our example we are trying to connect to MariaDB 10.11.13 which returns the func `MySQLMasterStatusQueryNew` and not the supported command in func `MySQLMasterStatusQuery`. 

The error surfaced associated with this is `Query 1 ERROR at Line 1: : You have an error in your SQL syntax; check the manual that corresponds to your MariaDB server version for the right syntax to use near 'LOG STATUS' at line 1`.

### Solution

Due to the compatibility between MariaDB and MySQL especially in the CDC space I wouldn't recommend cloning the driver and changing the version logic, I think the overhead there would be more than it's worth. 

The suggestion I had was to evaluate the Engine string within the pkg/jdbc/jdbc.go `MySQLVersion` function and resolve to the associated MariaDB version to MySQL for example in our instance:

MariaDB: `SELECT @@version` = 10.11.13-MariaDB-log

Within the `MySQLVersion` check for the string instance of `MariaDB` and if so present resolve to a MySQL version string. Ideally `10.11.13-MariaDB-log` would resolve to the `MySQLMas…

Issue (completed): ## Environment

- **Deploy method**: docker
- **Olake version**:  for instance `0.2.3`
- **OS**: official olake docker image 
- **Mongo version**: 6

## Description

MongoDB change streams accessed through mongos (MongoDB router) have non-blocking behavior where cursor.TryNext() immediately returns false even when change events are available, causing Change Data Capture (CDC) operations to miss document changes. This occurs regardless of the number of shards behind mongos and is specific to the mongos routing layer. 

## Steps to reproduce

I created a sample project to demonstrate the issue. https://github.com/dschaaff/olake-monogs-cdc-bug-repro. The docker compose stack it contains sets up mongo behind mongos and contains a script to demonstrate the behavior.

- olake initial sync backfill
- write mongo document
- run olake and observe cdc does not pickup new document
- write mongo document
- run olake and observe cdc does not pickup new document

## Expected behavior

CDC successfully returns new documents when connecting through mongos. 

## Actual behavior

Olake never syncs new documents beyond the initial backfill.

The issue appears to be that the MongoDB Go driver's TryNext() method behaves differently when connecting through mongos vs. direct replica set connections:

  1. Direct Replica Set: TryNext() has blocking behavior
  2. Via Mongos: TryNext() is non-blocking and may return false immediately even when events exist

https://pkg.go.dev/go.mongodb.org/mongo-driv…

- contributor: @dschaaff we will fix it in next 2 days. Thank you for reporting.

Could you please verify if this resolves your use case?

The issue occurs because, when connecting through mongos, the MongoDB Go driver’s non-blocking TryNext() can return false even when events exist. With the PBRT approach, we periodically checkpoint the latest stream position. These resume tokens are shard-safe, ensuring the CDC process reliably resumes without missing events.

text:
Issue (completed): ## Description
When running an incremental sync for the first time, Olake triggers a backfill before incremental to store initial cursor values.
Currently, in all drivers (Postgres, MySQL, Oracle), ChunkIterator opens a new transaction for each chunk.

This means that:
- Each SELECT * for a chunk runs under a different transaction.
- If new data is inserted/updated between chunk reads, incorrect chunk value is saved in state.
- The incremental sync may start from an incorrect cursor state.

Example scenario:
Backfill splits a table into 3 chunks with initial max cursor values:
```
Chunk 1: max cursor = 1  
Chunk 2: max cursor = 4  
Chunk 3: max cursor = 6  
```
While processing Chunk 2, some row from Chunk 1 changes so that its  max cursor is now 9, more changes happen in chunk 3 at same time so that its max cursor is now 10.
At the end of backfill, the saved cursor in state becomes 10 (the highest seen across all chunks).
Incremental sync will start from cursor >= 10, skipping rows that had cursor values between 6–9.

1. Start a first-time incremental sync on a table.
2. Observe that in backfill.go, for each chunk, driver. ChunkIterator starts its own transaction.
3. While backfill is running, update data in the table between chunk queries (specially for the cursor fields set).

## Description

The Olake MongoDB driver crashes with a panic during the backfill process when syncing a large collection (e.g., > 1 billion documents). The sync process fails immediately after connecting to the database, during the initial chunking phase.

The root cause of the error is in the `totalCountInCollection` function in `drivers/mongodb/internal/backfill.go`. page_title: GitHub issue olake#354: Enable Parallel Chunk Creation and Iteration to Improve Sync Performance
text:
Issue (completed): ### Problem

Currently, the chunking and iteration phases during the sync process are executed sequentially. First, all chunks for a table are created using a single database connection. Only after this phase is complete does the system begin iterating over and processing these chunks.

This design introduces two key limitations:

- Underutilization of database connections: While chunk creation is ongoing, only one database connection is used, regardless of the configured maximum.
- Slower sync performance: Since iteration waits for all chunks to be created, there is unnecessary delay.

### Solution

Introduce parallelization between chunk creation and chunk processing. The idea is to:

- Use one connection for chunk creation.
- As soon as a chunk is created, immediately hand it off to worker routines (using the remaining DB connections) for processing.
- Once all chunks are created, the initial chunking thread can also join the worker pool to help with remaining chunks.

This design will better utilize available DB connections and improve sync throughput by overlapping chunk creation and data extraction.

Issue (completed): ### Problem

Currently, Olake's sync process generates critical runtime artifacts such as `state.json`, which are essential for tracking sync progress and enabling resumption. These artifacts are stored only on the local filesystem where the Olake process is running.

This local-only storage presents several challenges:
1.  **State Loss & Difficult Resumption:** If the Olake process runs in an ephemeral environment (e.g., a Kubernetes pod that gets rescheduled, a temporary VM, or a CI runner) or if the local environment is lost, the state file is lost. This makes it impossible to reliably resume syncs from the last known point, potentially leading to data re-processing or data gaps.
2.  **Operational Complexity:** Managing state across distributed or dynamically provisioned instances becomes complex and error-prone.
3.  **Limited Debuggability & Auditing:** While not yet implemented for logs, the current architecture doesn't easily lend itself to persistently storing other artifacts like detailed logs, stats, or catalogs for long-term analysis, debugging across runs, or auditing.

This problem is important because robust state management and artifact persistence are crucial for:
*   **Data Integrity:** Ensuring syncs can be reliably resumed prevents data loss or duplication.
*   **Operational Efficiency:** Reduces manual intervention and re-processing time.
*   **Scalability & Resilience:** Enables Olake to run effectively in modern, distributed, and cloud-native environments…

Implement an "Append-Only" write mode in OLake that appends (inserts) records into the target table instead of modifying or deleting existing records. - Snapshot: A full snapshot of the table at a point in time.

- Enables audit logging and historical tracking of changes without modifying existing records.
- Supports downstream processing for CDC (Change Data Capture) workloads.
- Helps maintain immutability for compliance or analytical purposes.

**Configuration Options:**
- Add an optional parameter (e.g., write_mode: append_only) to enable this feature.

page_title: GitHub issue olake#151: improvement: Acknowledge Postgres LSN in batches
text:
Issue (completed): ## Problem
Currently, we only acknowledge the LSN after the entire sync is finished. While this works in many cases, it introduces a risk when the WAL logs are generated at a rate faster than we can read and process them.
If the assigned storage for WAL logs fills up before we finish syncing and acknowledge the final LSN, PostgreSQL might drop our cursor, leading to data loss or requiring a full resync.

## Proposed Solution:
- Acknowledge LSN in smaller batches during the sync process, not just at the end
- This allows PostgreSQL to safely drop older WAL logs in a timely manner
- Reduces pressure on WAL storage and provides more breathing room for the reader to keep up

page_title: GitHub issue olake-ui#93: Temporal Worker death results in Orphaned OLake containers
text:
Issue (completed): ## Environment

- **Deploy method**: Both docker-compose.yml and built from sources
- **Olake-UI version**:  all versions as of 20th june 2025
- **OS**: All OS
- **Cloud Provider**: All
- **Docker Params (if deployed with docker)**: N/A

## Description
When a temporal-worker crashes, the Docker container it launched (the OLake OG container) is not automatically terminated. This creates two critical problems:
 - Orphaned Containers: The original container continues to run, consuming host resources and writing data to the Iceberg tables.

 - Concurrent Execution: A Temporal retry will launch a new container for the same job, creating a race condition where two processes could be writing to the same destination, causing data duplication.

## Steps to reproduce

Steps to reproduce the behavior:
 - `cd olake-ui`
 - `docker compose up`
 - Create a Job and run it.
 - `docker stop olake-temporal-worker`
 - `docker ps` to see that the sync container is still running. It has now become an oprhan container(process).

## Expected behavior

When the temporal worker dies, all of the ***Activities triggered by it must also stop*** and ***before stopping the activities, the last state must be saved***.

## Actual behavior

Logically on the next schedule the sync will start from the last saved state in the database which has already been synced by the orphan container resulting in data duplication.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/faec0a4e-71f0-4f98-9a49-08ef9dd53fef)

Here are two potential approaches to solve this problem.

**Description:** In this approach, the worker will maintain a list of WorkflowID’s in the Postgres Database along with the container name it has spin up.

Add entry for WorkflowID and it’s corresponding ContainerID with status: "running" into the Postgres database immediately after starting the container.

Worker → PostgreSQL table:
| workflow_id | container_name | status  | created_at |
|-------------|----------------|---------|------------|
| sync-123    | olake-sync-123 | running | ...        |

The code uses dockerCmd.CombinedOutput() as stated in line 101 of file server/internal/docker/runner.go which blocks the execution i.e. does not move to next line of code unless it receives some output.

Once the response is received from line 101 we can decide on the row entry in database based on exit code.

 - If response is success(exit status 0), delete the row with WorkflowID from the database.

 - If the response is failer(exit status >0), mark the status column for the particular WorkflowID as failed meanwhile updating the state.json file…

page_title: GitHub issue olake-helm#231: Worker v0.4.0 image not published to Docker Hub — S3 log storage mode non-functional with chart 0.0.30
text:
Issue (completed): ## Summary

Chart `olake-helm 0.0.30` ships S3 log file storage support and documents it as the recommended mode going forward ([install/kubernetes docs](https://olake.io/docs/install/kubernetes/)). The docs state S3 mode requires:

> OLake Version 0.12.0 and above
> OLake UI 0.7.0 and above
> Helm chart 0.0.30 and above
> **OLake worker 0.4.0 and above**

Worker v0.4.0 was tagged + GitHub-released on 2026-10-08 (release [v0.4.0](https://github.com/datazip-inc/olake-helm/releases/tag/v0.4.0), notably bundling PR #189 "chore: added-s3"). However, **no `olakego/ui-worker:v0.4.0` image exists on Docker Hub.** Only `v0.3.11` (and `:latest`, which == `v0.3.11`, pushed 2026-09-10) are available as semver tags.

Result: an operator who follows the official S3-mode setup gets a Worker that is NOT S3-aware. The symptoms are confusing and non-obvious:

1. Chart renders fine, pods come up healthy.
2. Clicking "Create Source" in the UI hangs on 4 spinning dots.
3. UI backend returns `error in request /api/v1/project/.../sources/spec: failed to get spec: failed to extract workflow response: workflow execution failed: context canceled`.
4. Temporal workflow `fetch-spec-postgres-*` reports `COMPLETED` with result `{"response":"fetch-spec-postgres-<id>/output.json"}` — a RELATIVE PATH.
5. UI tries to read that path from its own emptyDir (`/tmp/olake-config/<id>/output.json`) and fails with `no such file or directory`.
6. The spec `output.json` only exists in Worker's own pod-local filesystem…

Discussion:

- collaborator: Thanks for the report, @aanandswitch, and sorry for the trouble. The v0.4.0 release build failed, so the image was never pushed. It is now on Docker Hub (amd64 + arm64):

`olakego/ui-worker:v0.4.0` = `latest` = `sha256:1675f67c...`

To pick it up, either:
- restart the worker: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/olake-workers -n <namespace>`. This pulls the new `latest` as long as you kept the chart default `pullPolicy: Always`.
- or pin `olakeWorker.image.tag: v0.4.0` and run `helm upgrade`.

You can drop the `dev-latest` workaround. That tag tracks unreleased dev builds.

#232 fixes the release build. Let us know if S3 mode works for you on v0.4.0.

page_title: GitHub issue olake-helm#117: Allow configuring the sync pod (source connector) image via Helm values
text:
Issue (completed): ## Description

The worker component hardcodes the source connector image prefix as `olakego/source` in Go code (`worker/constants/constants.go`). The sync pod image is always constructed as:

```
olakego/source-{sourceType}:{version}
```

There is no Helm values field to override this image, making it impossible to use custom or mirrored source connector images without external tooling.

## Use Case

When mirroring OLake images to a private registry (e.g. AWS ECR), the core component images (UI, worker, temporal, etc.) can be configured via `values.yaml`. However, the sync pod image — which is the most critical runtime component — cannot be configured through Helm at all.

This forces users to rely on external mutation mechanisms (e.g. Kyverno ClusterPolicy, OPA Gatekeeper, or admission webhooks) to rewrite the image at pod creation time:

```yaml
# Kyverno policy example to rewrite sync pod image
mutate:
  patchStrategicMerge:
    spec:

page_title: GitHub issue olake-helm#116: Registry prefix incorrectly prepended to fully-qualified image URLs
text:
Issue (completed): ## Description

The chart unconditionally prepends `registryBase` (defaulting to `registry-1.docker.io`) to all user-configurable image repositories. This breaks deployments that use non-Docker-Hub registries such as AWS ECR, GCR, or GHCR.

## Steps to Reproduce

Set any component image to a fully-qualified registry URL:

```yaml
olakeUI:
  image:
    repository: 123456789012.dkr.ecr.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com/olake-ui
    tag: v0.3.2
```

The rendered manifest produces:

```
image: "registry-1.docker.io/123456789012.dkr.ecr.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com/olake-ui:v0.3.2"
```

This causes `ErrImagePull` on all affected pods.

## Root Cause

The `olake.registryBase` helper in `_helpers.tpl` always returns a registry prefix, and all templates unconditionally prepend it:

```
image: "{{ include "olake.registryBase" . }}/{{ .Values.olakeUI.image.repository }}:{{ .Values.olakeUI.image.tag }}"
```

There is no way to opt out of this prefix when the repository is already a fully-qualified URL.

## Affected Templates

- `olake-ui/deployment.yaml`
- `olake-worker/deployment.yaml`
- `temporal/deployment.yaml`
- `elasticsearch/deployment.yaml`
- `postgresql/deployment.yaml`

## Current Workaround

Using a Helm post-renderer that strips the `registry-1.docker.io/` prefix via `sed`.

## Proposed Fix

See PR #115 — adds an `olake.imageRef` helper that detects fully-qualified repositories (first path segment contains a `.`) and skips the prefix, while preserving backwards compatibility for Docker Hub…

Discussion:

- contributor: Hi @osalloum this is not the case.
```
The CONTAINER_REGISTRY_BASE feature is intentionally a global registry mirror prefix — not a Docker Hub URL that gets prepended to a "fully-qualified" repository. The design is:

  <CONTAINER_REGISTRY_BASE> + "/" + <image.repository> + ":" + <tag>

  Where image.repository is meant to be the image path within your chosen registry, not a fully-qualified URL.

  Correct Usage for ECR (or any private registry)

  Instead of putting the full ECR URL in repository, set CONTAINER_REGISTRY_BASE to your ECR registry and keep repository as the relative image path:

  global:
    env:
      CONTAINER_REGISTRY_BASE: "123456789012.dkr.ecr.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com"

  olakeUI:
    image:
      repository: olake-ui        # or your mirror path, e.g. "dockerhub-mirror/olakego/ui"
      tag: v0.3.2

  This renders as: 123456789012.dkr.ecr.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com/olake-ui:v0.3.2 ✅

  This is the same pattern shown in our README for air-gapped ECR deployments:
  global:
    env:
      CONTAINER_REGISTRY_BASE: "1234567890123.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/dockerhub_mirror"
```
